userStories.title: CRITICAL — retirement-migration integration test RED in CI (skills.slug undefined); migration scope-safety UNVERIFIED, required orchestrator-tests check failing
userStories.description: REVIEW FINDING (adversarial review 2026-08-28). The REQUIRED orchestrator-tests CI job has been RED on every push since US-021 (runs 33162512949 US-021, 33163126563 US-022, 33163986823 scope-guard — all fail identically). Root cause: tests/test_prd222_retirement_migration.py:131 runs `INSERT INTO skills (name, slug) VALUES ('t', :sl)` but the skills table has NO `slug` column — core/models/core.py:359-394 defines name + skill_type (NOT NULL, :365) + package_slug (:380); there is no bare `slug`. CI error verbatim: `sqlalchemy.exc.ProgrammingError: (psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn) column "slug" of relation "skills" does not exist`. The test dies at FIXTURE SETUP (line 131) BEFORE it executes any migration DELETE (lines 141-144) or any assertion (lines 150-156). Consequences: (a) required CI check red = merge blocker; (b) the CRITICAL scope-safety property this @integration test exists to prove — seeded onboarding agents removed while a non-onboarding system agent AND a normal user agent SURVIVE, plus FK-safe agent_skills cleanup and idempotent re-run — is UNVERIFIED in CI; the pure chain/scope tests pass but none exercise real rows. (c) The US-021 AC ('orchestrator full suite 4292 passed at documented baseline... @integration test proving seeded row removed... CI runs it') and US-022 AC ('4292 passed... documented baseline UNCHANGED') are FALSE: the builder ran locally where this @integration test SKIPS (engine fixture skip at :98, no local Postgres), so the failure only surfaces in CI where Postgres is present. Note: the migration SQL itself is schema-valid — all columns it touches were verified to exist (agent_skills.agent_id core.py:32, workflow_agents.agent_id core.py:39, workflow_executions.agent_id core.py:569, agents.is_system_agent/required_role core.py:260-261) — so this is a broken-TEST + red-CI + false-green finding, NOT a migration-crashes-on-deploy one. But the safety net that proves the delete cannot over-reach is down.
